_comment: Synthetic DE-301 case where applicant != appointee. Petitioner (sister of decedent) is asking the court to appoint a corporate trustee (Bath Savings Trust Co.) as PR — common when the estate is complex or contentious. Demonstrates that applicant_full_legal_name and person_whose_appointment_is_sought are DIFFERENT — the pipeline must NOT duplicate.

appointee_record.appointee: Bath Savings Trust Company, by James L. Hartwell, Trust Officer
appointee_record._note: Appointee is a corporate trustee, not a natural person. The form's person_whose_appointment_is_sought accepts an entity name; the trust officer is identified parenthetically.

venue._note: Decedent domiciled in Kennebec County — venue under § 3-201

will_posture.will_details: Will dated 2009-07-12 with codicils dated 2014-03-08 and 2019-11-22; both codicils witnessed and self-proved.
will_posture._note: Decedent's will named his late wife as PR (predeceased him in 2022); successor PR nomination was contingent on his children, none of whom are willing or able to serve. Will permits the court to appoint any qualified successor.

appointment_sought.person_whose_appointment_is_sought: Bath Savings Trust Company, by James L. Hartwell, Trust Officer
appointment_sought._reason_for_corporate_trustee: Estate has 14 disputed heirs (two prior marriages + cohabiting partner + adopted stepchildren), commercial real estate holdings in three counties, an active business interest (Tilton Tractor Sales, 51% ownership), and an ongoing wrongful-death action where decedent was the defendant. Family agreement: corporate trustee minimizes intra-family conflict and has the operational capacity to manage the business.

relationships.applicant_to_decedent: sister — one of 4 surviving siblings; not an heir under the will (decedent had children) but is interested party as the sibling who organized the family agreement
relationships.other_heirs: Five surviving adult children (2 from first marriage, 3 from second), cohabiting partner Margaret O. Tilton (not a registered domestic partner under Maine law), four adopted stepchildren from the second marriage — all named/served separately.

_what_this_exercises_beyond_case_example: applicant != appointee (the central distinction from case.example.json)
Corporate appointee — non-natural-person value for person_whose_appointment_is_sought
nominated_as_pr_in_will=no — the negative branch of the testate posture
applicant_legal_interest='heir' — but the applicant is NOT being appointed; she's just the interested-party petitioner
Validators expected to NOT fire on equals_field for person_whose_appointment_is_sought (no such rule encoded) but the pipeline must understand the difference
applicant_signature_name STILL matches applicant_full_legal_name (Rebecca, not Bath Savings) — the applicant is the affiant signing the petition
notary_appearer_name STILL matches applicant_full_legal_name — Rebecca is the one appearing before the notary
